status: source-version sequence reconciliation; not diplomatic native-script transcription
inspection: Both complete native pages visually read against complete aligned Roman/English sequence. Same title, narrative blocks, participants and beginning/end confirmed. Roman readings remain pending high-resolution second review.

blocks.evidence: One man, two sons; younger son asks his father for property share; division between two.
Younger son departs to distant country, wastes property, famine and poverty, swine keeping, hunger, resolve to return and confession.
Father sees returning son, embrace and kisses, son confession, clothes/ring/shoes, rejoicing over son alive again.
Elder son returns from field, hears singing/dancing, asks servant, learns brother returned; native page ends at thy father.
Feast, angry elder son refuses entry, father entreats, elder complains of service without small goat and younger wasting possessions.
Father negates complaint: always with me; all mine thine; brother was dead and now living, lost and found.

installation_policy: Use exact aligned Roman attestations and printed English glosses. Do not infer native-script forms or duplicate attestations from the alternate presentation. No extra lexical list or unmatched narrative block observed on native pages.
limitations: Sequence and block reconciliation does not prove every native character is identical to Roman representation. No native diplomatic transcription claimed.
